newsitem.title: CANADA: Belgian brewer set to sell Toronto Blue Jays - paper.
newsitem.headline: Belgian brewer set to sell Toronto Blue Jays - paper.

text.p: Belgian brewer Interbrew SA has made a formal application to Major League Baseball for permission to sell the two-time World Series champions Toronto Blue Jays baseball team, the Toronto Star reported on Friday.
The newspaper said Interbrew put forward the name of at least one potential buyer for consideration by baseball authorities, a group headed by Toronto dentist-turned-property-developer Murray Frum.

The price tag being considered is as much as one-third lower than the $152 million the team was originally believed to be worth, the Toronto Star said. It also quoted sources as saying the price under consideration was at least $30 million or $40 million lower than the owners hoped for.

New York-based "Financial World" magazine had estimated the Blue Jays would fetch $152 million. Interbrew acquired 90 percent of the Jays as part of its acquisition of Labatt Breweries last year for $1.58 billion. The remaining 10 percent is held by Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce.

Informal talks between Interbrew and two buyers, Frum's group and a team backed by Perfund Management Ltd., had been ongoing for some time, the newspaper said. It said the formal application was an important step in a process that may still take months.
Officials have to approve any prospective buyers before they will give out detailed financial information about the club.
